root_idea.summary: The root has two principal orientations: bringing something from one place to another, and a covering or layer that envelops something.
root_idea.development: The bringing sense extends to attracting, procuring, mustering, and the agents or goods involved in transport. The covering sense includes skin coverings and the garment called جِلْبَاب.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Distinct Quran-attested nominal, normalized from the Quranic plural to the singular citation form.

senses.definition: To raise a clamour against an adversary, calling out with or bringing up one's forces against them.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic imperative construction أَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِمْ, the action is directed against them and is associated with forces on horseback and on foot.

senses.definition: To muster forces against someone and threaten them with evil; to cause forces to act in concert against them.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an alternative Quranic interpretation of the construction أَجْلِبْ عَلَيْهِمْ, emphasizing collection and hostile intimidation rather than the raising of cries.

senses.definition: An outer garment or enveloping wrap used to cover the body, head, or bosom.
senses.usage_conditions: The Quranic form is the plural جَلَابِيب, referring to women's outer coverings; the singular citation form is جِلْبَاب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To drive, bring, convey, or transport people, animals, goods, or merchandise from one place to another, especially for trade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be a single thing or a group; the expression also occurs in discussions of bringing cattle to a collector or market.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To draw, attract, or procure something toward oneself.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used figuratively of things that bring friends, benefits, or misfortunes.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To urge a racehorse onward by cries, chiding, striking, or by following or leading another horse behind it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional racing usage, including the practice of using a person, horse, or object to urge a competing horse toward the finish.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To earn or procure provisions for one's family and to manage one's affairs resourcefully.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression may imply purveying or exercising skill and practical ingenuity in family provision.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To raise cries, shouts, or confused noise; to make a clamour.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the general noise-making use, distinct from the hostile Quranic construction represented under أَجْلَبَ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To commit a crime or punishable offense against someone.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عَلَى before the person against whom the offense is committed.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a wound or ulcer, to heal and become covered with skin; of blood, to dry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The healing and drying applications are grouped as related results of forming a covering or becoming dry.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a company or troop, to assemble or become collected together.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Intransitive use referring to a group that gathers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The act of bringing together or collecting.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A verbal noun of Form II, denoting the causative or completed act of gathering things together.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to bring forth male offspring.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage contrasted with أَحْلَبَ, to bring forth females.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To aid, help, or assist another.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Classical Form IV usage, separate from its hostile Quranic construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put an amulet into a skin case.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The amulet case is associated with a horse's trappings or similar equipment.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To cover a camel's saddle with a piece of fresh skin and leave it to dry and tighten.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The construction takes the saddle as its object and refers to a skin covering called جُلْبَة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To be driven or brought from one place or country to another, especially for sale.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to animals, captives, slaves, or merchandise in an intransitive or passive-like construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a poet, to take or borrow material from another poet's poetry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of bringing something in from elsewhere.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek or demand a thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object is understood from context and need not be a transported commodity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To seek, demand, or desire that animals, captives, slaves, or merchandise be brought from elsewhere.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The desired result is the transport of the specified object to the seeker's location or for sale.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put a garment called جِلْبَاب on another person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Transitive clothing construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To put on or cover oneself with a جِلْبَاب or other garment.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reflexive or intransitive clothing construction, applicable to a man or woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The blackness of night.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use, sometimes treated as figurative in the lexical discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel saddle of the kind called رَحْل, including its cover, wooden parts, or curved wooden parts.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote the whole saddle or one of its specified components, according to context.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thin or waterless cloud, including a cloud extending across the horizon like a mountain or mountain range.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The cloud may be described as narrow, distant, or darkening; its lack of water is part of some definitions.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Animals, goods, or merchandise brought from one place to another for sale; also transport camels carrying people's goods.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This noun is also used for the camels or loads brought to a person at a water or settlement; جَلُوبَة is explicitly treated as a synonym or related form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Male camels brought or driven for sale.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal application connected with the practice of driving them from place to place.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Persons who drive or bring camels, sheep, goats, or other goods from one place or country to another for sale.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural may refer to a group of such animal or merchandise drivers.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Cries, shouts, noises, or a confused mixture of sounds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use for clamour or noisy confusion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An assembly of men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use related to the sense of gathering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The small piece of skin, crust, or scab that forms over a healing wound.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is جُلَب.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A piece of skin placed upon a camel's saddle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: It may serve as a covering or be left to dry over the saddle; this is distinct from the wound scab sense.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A skin case for an amulet, or an amulet with a piece of skin sewn upon it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The object may be the case itself or the amulet equipped with that covering.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A detached portion of cloud or a cloud covering the sky.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A cloud formation sense related to the covering or overlying branch of the root.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A patch of ground differing from the land adjoining it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Synonymous with بُقْعَة in this application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A detached portion of herbage or pasture.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Refers to an isolated patch of grazing or vegetation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Severity, pressure, hunger, adversity, or a hard and distressful year.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word may denote the vehemence of hunger or the general severity of circumstances.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Dominion, sovereignty, or rule with which a person is invested.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative application of the garment or covering terminology.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A certain pulse or grain, including the seed known as خُلَّر and the common lathyrus or chickling vetch.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A collective plant name with several dialectal pronunciations and forms.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A leather case or scabbard-like container for a sword, whip, implements, or other weapons.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: جُلُبَّان السلاح may include the case and its contents, or weapons requiring effort to draw rather than a lance.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A clamorous man or one who makes confused cries or noise.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A personal noun derived from the noise-making branch.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person, especially a slave, brought from one place or country to another for sale.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to a man or woman; one usage specifies arrival in Muslim territory.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An acquired or affected habit or disposition.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An explicitly figurative application.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Rose-water.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An Arabicized loanword, lexically distinct from the root's native branches.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A woman who is clamorous, noisy, very garrulous, or ill-natured; a related form may describe someone rude and coarse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source explicitly applies this personal noun to a woman.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A cause or means of bringing, drawing, attracting, or procuring something.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural may denote causes through which events or benefits are brought about.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Calamities, misfortunes, adverse events, or difficulties.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative plural use for things that bring adversity.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A person who puts an amulet into a skin case and sews it onto a horse's trappings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized occupational or functional noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Boisterous, applied to thunder or rain.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A descriptive participial use for loud or tumultuous weather.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bead, gem, or similar stone used as a charm to captivate someone, restore affection, or bring back a person after flight.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A traditional desert charm; the source also reports a view that this item is quadriliteral.

cautions: The Quranic command in 17:64 has two explicitly recorded lexical interpretations: raising a hostile clamour with forces, and mustering forces while threatening the adversary. The nominal Quranic form جَلَابِيب is presented under its singular citation form جِلْبَاب.
unassigned_or_ambiguous_evidence: lane-unit:jlb:47084:g1:main reports a Form V gloss attributed to Golius, but the lexical source explicitly states that the gloss cannot be found in the cited lexicons; it is therefore not assigned a dictionary meaning.
